clue.text: Roll back around whistle-blower's house

indicators.note: around says the roll's letters sit either side of the referee
back tells us the roll's word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
the referee, REF for short, is the one who blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: A bread roll tucked round the house of someone who exposes wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests someone who leaks secrets; here it is the match official. 'back' turns the roll round and 'around' wraps it about the official.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated dwelling, an example of a house built from factory-made sections.

clue.text: Give new energy to record-breaking oarsman

indicators.note: the record breaking into the oarsman means it is put inside that word

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A rowing champion who has smashed a record is given fresh energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record-breaking' reads as a single sporting adjective; it splits into a record and a signal that the record breaks into the oarsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To repower something is to fit it with a fresh source of power, so to give it new energy.

clue.text: Cockney Chuck's suddenly stopped

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker turns a TH sound into F, so the word is heard in that London accent

parts.note: chuck's means throws, as in chucks or tosses

explanation.surface: A Londoner called Chuck abruptly comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name but is the verb: 'chuck's' gives THROWS. Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which pronounces TH as F, so THROWS becomes 'frows'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who froze stopped moving all at once, as if turned to ice.

clue.text: Squash bullies' leader — complete lunatic

indicators.note: the leader of bullies is the first letter of that word

parts.note: complete, as in a complete fool, means utter
a nut is a crazy person, a lunatic

explanation.surface: A squash player at the front of a gang of bullies is a total maniac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' sounds like the verb or the racket sport; it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut is a variety of winter squash with a pale beige skin and orange flesh.

clue.text: Start to draft a report about water from the Eye

indicators.note: about signals that the gathered letters are moved around into a new order
the start to draft is that word's first letter

explanation.surface: Begin writing up a report on the water around the London Eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' but is the anagram signal for D plus A plus REPORT. The capital in 'Eye' hints at the London Eye beside the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single drop of the salty liquid that the eye sheds when crying.

clue.text: Pedal expert read legal parts

indicators.note: parts says the letters are taken as a part spanning those words

explanation.surface: A specialist studied sections of the law about a pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across expeRT READ LEgal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever, a pedal, as on an old sewing machine.

clue.text: Record company's software extremely laughable

parts.note: an app is a piece of software

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of laughable

explanation.surface: A record label's computer programs are utterly ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple Records was the label founded by the Beatles in 1968.

clue.text: Abandon targets for rugby scores

parts.note: to drop something is to abandon it
goals are aims or targets

explanation.surface: Giving up on aims in favour of points scored in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a drop goal, kicked after the ball bounces, scores three points.

clue.text: Put too much in round barrel before getting in

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: getting in says the word for before goes inside the barrel

parts.note: a vat is a large barrel or tub
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Filling a round barrel too full before climbing into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put too much in' sounds like overfilling the barrel; it means stuffing too much into oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to take in more food than one needs, so putting too much in one's stomach.

clue.text: Shoot French author's son in the head

indicators.note: in the head says the son's letter is moved to the very front of the word

parts.note: Marcel Proust was the French author of In Search of Lost Time

explanation.surface: Sounds like a call to shoot a French writer's boy in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a violent order; it is the plant noun. PROUST already holds S: moving it to the start gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a new growth from a plant, the same as a shoot.

clue.text: Blows up former policeman at test centre

parts.note: ex means former
Plod is British slang for a policeman, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books

indicators.note: the centre of test is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: A former officer loses his temper at a testing facility.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOD is British slang for the police, from PC Plod in the Noddy children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode is to burst violently, which is to blow up.

clue.text: Maybe Saturday night beginning dangerously with little knowledge in Glasgow

parts.note: wee means small or little, especially in Scotland
ken is the Scots word for knowledge, as used in Glasgow

indicators.note: the beginning of dangerously is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wild Saturday night out in Glasgow, starting with risky behaviour on little information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks Saturday night as only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday night is part of the leisure days at the end of the working week, an example of it.

clue.text: League's ruined without uniform golf scores

indicators.note: ruined says the letters left are wrecked into a new order
without says the uniform letter is taken out of the word for the league

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf league is in ruins after its players lose their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle in golf is a score two strokes under par on a hole.

clue.text: Penny submits additional business proposal for Charles Edward Stuart and Perkin Warbeck?

definitions.text: Charles Edward Stuart and Perkin Warbeck?
definitions.note: the question mark shows these two men are examples of the plural answer

parts.note: someone who re-tenders puts in a fresh bid or offer for business

explanation.surface: Someone named Penny bids again for a contract, and two historical claimants are named.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Edward Stuart (Bonnie Prince Charlie) and Perkin Warbeck both claimed the English throne without success.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men were claimants to a throne not theirs, the classic examples of royal pretenders.

clue.text: Dons resort to puns

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: University teachers fall back on wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' suggests Oxbridge academics; it is the verb meaning puts clothes on. 'resort' is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: To don a garment is to put it on, so dons means pulls on clothing.

clue.text: Farron and Henman face off over priest setting deadline

indicators.note: over is used in the sense of round, so the two names go round the priest

parts.note: Tim Farron is a former Liberal Democrat leader

indicators.note: face off says the two names confront each other, so the second one is written facing the opposite way

parts.note: Tim Henman is a former British tennis player
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A politician and a tennis player confront each other over a cleric, with a cut-off looming.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Farron led the UK Liberal Democrats; Tim Henman was a leading British tennis player. 'face off' turns the second name round to face the first, and 'over' means round here.
explanation.definitionFit: A time limit is the latest point by which something must be done, which is a deadline.

clue.text: Cutting off home counties raven flying around church

parts.note: the home counties lie in the South East of England, SE

indicators.note: flying around suggests the bird's letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A raven circles a church and cuts off the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance is the act of severing, cutting something off or ending a connection.

clue.text: Workers possibly like collecting books

indicators.note: collecting says the word for like gathers the books inside it

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Employees who enjoy gathering books together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells us worker ants are only one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are sterile female insects that do the colony's labour, so ants are examples of workers.

clue.text: See 13
Those people show what Donald Trup is missing

parts.note: what here points to a particular thing, the definite article placed before the missing letter
the printed surname lacks one letter of the President's real name, so the missing piece is that letter

explanation.surface: A misspelt politician's name exposes something absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trup' looks like a typo, but it is the point: the familiar surname has lost its M, so what is missing is 'the M'.
explanation.definitionFit: Them is the object pronoun for those people other than ourselves.

clue.text: Warm woman, Erica?

definitions.note: the question mark shows the plant genus is a definition by example

parts.note: to heat something is to warm it
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman called Erica is warmed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erica' looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical genus of heaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of flowering shrubs whose common name is heath or ling.

clue.text: Set new levies on it

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A government fixing fresh taxes on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb about fixing taxes; it is the noun, a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is short for a receiving set, so a television is a set.

clue.text: Strangely sullen about uniform with small crescents

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the uniform letter
strangely says the letters of sullen are shaken into an odd order

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier sulking in his uniform, decorated with tiny crescents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the anagram of SULLEN round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunules are small crescent-shaped marks, like the pale half-moon at a fingernail's base.

clue.text: Travelling partition moves when it isn't there

indicators.note: moves says the remaining letters are shifted into a new order
isn't there says the two-letter word it is missing from the word partition

explanation.surface: A dividing wall gets shifted around while nobody is present.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTITION without IT leaves PARTION, which 'moves' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a trip means away on a journey, which is travelling.

clue.text: Trouble very much engulfs Republican rating

indicators.note: engulfs says the word for very much swallows the trouble inside it

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you'

explanation.surface: A political scandal swamps a Republican's poll ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a poll score; in the Royal Navy a rating is an ordinary sailor without officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned member of a navy's crew, an enlisted seaman.

clue.text: Crèche wasting hours making preliminary survey

indicators.note: making says the leftover letters are worked into a new word
wasting hours says the hours are lost from the nursery's word

explanation.surface: A nursery that fritters away time on an initial inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking H out of CRECHE leaves CRECE, which 'making' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Recce is military slang for reconnaissance, a preliminary survey of an area.

clue.text: Enlightened state strangely invariant without outsiders

indicators.note: strangely says what is left is jumbled into an odd new order
without outsiders drops the first and last letters of invariant

explanation.surface: An unchanging condition of enlightenment, strangely without anyone outside.
explanation.walkthrough: INVARIANT without its outer I and T leaves NVARIAN, which 'strangely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the final state of enlightenment, free from desire and suffering.

clue.text: Chasing a queen underfoot

parts.note: foot is abbreviated FT, and under places the queen beneath it
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A queen being pursued gets trampled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underfoot' is two parts: 'foot' gives FT and 'under' puts ER below it in the down light. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Being after someone means pursuing them, so chasing them.

clue.text: Caught Alchemi cycling in compound?

indicators.note: in says the caught letter goes inside the cycled name
cycling says the setter's name has letters moved round from front to back

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The setter Alchemi is caught riding a bike inside an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: Alchemi is the setter's own pseudonym. 'cycling' carries its first two letters to the end, and 'in' puts the caught letter inside. 'compound?' looks like an enclosure; it is the substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical compound is a substance formed of two or more elements, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Reject article essentially congratulating disagreeable personality

indicators.note: reject is read as re-ject, throwing back, so the article is written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: essentially picks the essence, the central letters, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Turning down an article that praises an unpleasant character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns AN into NA; 'essentially' takes TU from the middle of 'congratulating' and RE from the middle of 'disagreeable'. 'disagreeable' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's nature is their basic character and temperament, their personality.

clue.text: Monks regularly defrost soup in advance

indicators.note: in advance says the soup comes before the other letters

parts.note: broth is a thin soup

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of defrost

explanation.surface: Monks routinely thaw their soup ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of dEfRoSt give ERS, with BROTH put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks in a religious order address each other as brothers, a term for male members.

clue.text: Regret going back to work with Earl in a lot of countries

indicators.note: going back says the word for regret is read from end to start

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A nobleman regrets returning to a job in a land of many nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is the continent made up of some fifty nations, a lot of countries.
